findings.title: Wager atomicity is a compensating saga, not one transaction
findings.observed: Buy-ins are debited seat by seat. A failure refunds already-applied debits and records refund-failed evidence. Table cashouts pay seat by seat and roll back on failure. The escrow record is written only after the loop, so a reload or crash mid-loop leaves debits without an escrow record (recoverable only from TransactionEngine audit entries carrying the escrowId). Failure handling is careful and tested (G22), but this is not the 'whole trade fails' atomicity OSI asks for.
findings.intendedOwnership: TransactionEngine (OSI: atomic where possible).
findings.proposedSolution: Owner decides whether compensating sagas satisfy 'atomic where possible'. If not, add a TransactionEngine multi-actor adjustment (all deltas validated, applied and verified as one operation), shared with Holonet payouts (F-HOL-002). At minimum, persist an 'escrowing' state with the escrowId before the first debit.
findings.regressionTests: tests/ti4c0-g22-wager-refund-replay.test.mjs, plus an interrupted-escrow test.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Reload the GM client during escrow; inspect the ledger.
findings.simplificationBenefit: One multi-party credit primitive across Holonet and games.

findings.title: Party Fund is a credit pool and ledger outside TransactionEngine
findings.observed: The fund balance is a world setting written with game.settings.set. Its ledger is a separate world setting truncated to 100 entries. Fund-side changes do not go through TransactionEngine; actor-side changes do. A job payout with a party cut writes the fund and then pays actors inside Holonet's own atomic wrapper.
findings.intendedOwnership: Undecided: OSI says TransactionEngine is the single source of truth with no parallel ledgers, while V-P6C-19 approves a Party Fund workflow with its own ledger entry.
findings.proposedSolution: Owner decides whether the Party Fund becomes a TransactionEngine-managed account (one ledger, atomic with actor deltas) or is a documented A-10 exception. Until then, no new Party Fund writers.
findings.alternatives: Model the fund as a world 'party' actor so TransactionEngine handles it as an ordinary actor.
findings.regressionTests: tests/ti4c0-g26-party-fund-integrity.test.mjs
findings.foundryAcceptance: Party Fund contribute/charge/payout plus vehicle ammo purchase.

findings.title: Party Fund ammunition debit outside TransactionEngine (owner workflow vs A-10); notification via raw ChatMessage
findings.observed: GM approval settles by PartyFundAccess.setBalance + appendLedger, then delivers; failure restores the snapshot; unprovable restore -> indeterminate. Owner-approved as workflow V-P6C-19, but A-10 (OSI) says TransactionEngine is the single credit authority with no parallel ledgers. Whisper uses globalThis.ChatMessage.create (A-05).
findings.intendedOwnership: A-10: TransactionEngine owns all credit movement including party funds.
findings.proposedSolution: Owner decides whether Party Fund is in A-10 scope. If yes: add a TransactionEngine party-fund transaction (debit + ledger + delivery callback) and route this settlement through it. Route the whisper through SWSEChat.
findings.alternatives: Record Party Fund as a documented A-10 exception owned by holonet.
findings.regressionTests: Existing p51/p52/p53 tests plus a test that settlement calls TransactionEngine.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Live V13: approve Party Fund request; forced delivery failure restores fund.

findings.title: A-03 probe hits are sanctioned in-memory derived writers (path conflict only)
findings.observed: xp-engine.computeXpDerived writes system.derived.xp in memory and is called only from SWSEV2BaseActor._performDerivedCalculation (prepare phase). ActorEngine._applyDerivedUpdates folds DerivedCalculator output in memory and shares the derived-generation stamp. Neither persists derived data. xp-engine.js also contains applyXP (a writer via ActorEngine), so the module mixes calculator and mutation roles.
findings.intendedOwnership: Derived writers live under scripts/actors/** or are explicitly listed in A-03.
findings.proposedSolution: Move computeXpDerived to scripts/actors/derived/xp-derived.js (pure) and keep applyXP in progression; amend A-03 to name ActorEngine._applyDerivedUpdates as the sanctioned fold. Owner decides the A-03 wording.
findings.alternatives: Amend A-03 only.
findings.regressionTests: Existing XP display tests; add a test that computeXpDerived has no ActorEngine import.

findings.title: Finalization is one transactional plan plus non-atomic post-commit writes
findings.observed: After applyMutationPlan, maneuver suite sync, ability-increase verification marker and certification are separate ActorEngine.updateActor calls; failures are surfaced (postApplyIncomplete / committed-unverified), not rolled back. All go through ActorEngine. This is a deliberate, documented design (comments at progression-finalizer.js:3970-3975) but contradicts the "commits once" wording.
findings.intendedOwnership: ActorEngine
findings.proposedSolution: Amend A-15/progression-architecture wording to "one transactional plan + idempotent post-commit evidence writes"; optionally fold maneuver sync into the plan.

findings.title: A-03 xp-engine derived writes are a legitimate delegated calculator
findings.observed: computeXpDerived writes system.derived.xp on the in-memory system object and is called only from the V2 base actor prepare. Legitimate; A-03 path wording should include delegated calculators.
findings.intendedOwnership: actor-core prepare (delegated)
findings.proposedSolution: Amend A-03 path to "invoked from V2 actor prepare"; optionally move file to scripts/actors/derived.

findings.title: Managed-effect expiry writes owned ActiveEffects directly
findings.observed: disableExpiredEffectsOnDocument calls document.updateEmbeddedDocuments("ActiveEffect", ...) on the actor and on each owned item, from combat turn-start/combat-end hooks (GM only). This bypasses ActorEngine.updateActiveEffects (actor-engine.js:4203) and its normalization/recalc; no @mutation-exception comment.
findings.intendedOwnership: Owned AE changes go through ActorEngine (A-02).
findings.proposedSolution: Route actor effects through ActorEngine.updateActiveEffects(actor, updates) and owned-item effects through an ActorEngine owned-item effect helper (add one if missing) with source "swse-basic-effect-*".
findings.alternatives: Document as exception (not recommended: owned docs).
findings.regressionTests: Unit test with fake ActorEngine: expiry calls updateActiveEffects, never document.updateEmbeddedDocuments.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Turn-start expiry in a live combat with GM and player clients.
findings.risk: Low; active effects are a runtime-risk area.

findings.title: Lineage credit awards bypass TransactionEngine and SWSEChat
findings.observed: _applyCreditsUpdate reads system.credits and writes credits+N through ActorEngine.updateActor; _notifyCreditsGranted posts ChatMessage.create directly. TransactionEngine.executeCreditAdjustment exists (scripts/engine/store/transaction-engine.js:557). Live via progression-engine.js and finalize-integration.js.
findings.intendedOwnership: Credit movement through TransactionEngine (A-10); gameplay chat through SWSEChat (A-05).
findings.proposedSolution: Replace _applyCreditsUpdate with TransactionEngine.executeCreditAdjustment (grant, source = ability) and _notifyCreditsGranted with SWSEChat (or the store receipt hook swseCreditGrantComplete which already renders a card, scripts/chat/store-receipt-chat.js:414). Amount and trigger unchanged.
findings.regressionTests: Test: lineage grant creates one TransactionEngine adjustment and no direct updateActor credit write.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Level-up with Lineage talent in Foundry.
findings.risk: Medium: credits and progression finalization are runtime-risk areas.

findings.title: A-05 bypassed at 74 live sites; probe misses the createChatMessage wrapper route
findings.observed: P-A05 counts 43 ChatMessage.create sites in 23 live modules (largest species-activated-ability-engine 12). In addition 17 live modules call document-api-v13 createChatMessage directly (31 sites: combat 8 files, feats 5, skills, rolls, ui-shell, species), bypassing SWSEChat card building, speaker and roll-mode handling.
findings.intendedOwnership: All gameplay chat through SWSEChat (A-05).
findings.proposedSolution: Extend P-A05 to count createChatMessage outside swse-chat. Reroute per owner domain to SWSEChat.postHTML/postRoll/cards, starting with the 12-site species engine and combat. Add a lint/census ratchet.
findings.regressionTests: Census ratchet; per-module tests with a fake SWSEChat.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Card appearance and whisper behaviour per rerouted flow.

findings.title: Force Alchemy debits credits outside TransactionEngine (A-10)
findings.observed: Credits are debited (441) and compensated (476) with ActorEngine.updateActor on a path chosen by a six-way heuristic (creditUpdatePath, 78-86) - a second credit schema interpretation. Line 462 (the probe hit) only builds the in-memory result payload: false positive. TransactionEngine already exposes executeCreditAdjustment (557) and executeMutationTransaction (308). The DSS+credit single write and inverse-delta compensation are deliberate (integration matrix :260) but not routed through the credit authority.
findings.intendedOwnership: TransactionEngine for the credit leg (OSI).
findings.proposedSolution: Use TransactionEngine.executeMutationTransaction for credits + DSS (it is the documented path when credits and actor mutation must succeed together); keep the FP V2 receipt leg; delete creditUpdatePath in favour of the TransactionEngine credit path.
findings.alternatives: executeCreditAdjustment for credits and a separate DSS write (loses the single write).
findings.regressionTests: class-force-v2-alchemy-atomicity extended for TransactionEngine routing.
findings.risk: Changes failure semantics of an accepted design

findings.title: Follower hotfixes write owner-actor flags directly and non-atomically
findings.observed: owner.setFlag("foundryvtt-swse","followerSlots") then a second setFlag("followers") - two persisted writes outside ActorEngine; a failure between them leaves slots and roster inconsistent. Entitlement repair writes followerSlots on ready.
findings.intendedOwnership: Owner actor state through ActorEngine (A-02), one write per logical change.
findings.proposedSolution: Replace with one ActorEngine.updateActor(owner, {"flags.foundryvtt-swse.followerSlots":..., "flags.foundryvtt-swse.followers":...}) call; then fold the logic into npc-followers.
findings.regressionTests: Fake-ActorEngine test: transfer produces one update with both keys.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Follower transfer when owner deleted, in Foundry.

findings.title: Chargen Summary stages credits and a store flag on the actor before finalization, outside TransactionEngine
findings.observed: enterStore() calls ActorEngine.updateActor with system.credits and flags.swse.chargenStore mid-wizard, then opens the live store against the actor. Finalization later reads the actor balance back through two copies of the same reconciliation (ProgressionFinalizer._resolveFinalStartingCredits and economy builder resolveFinalStartingCredits). The code comment at summary-step.js:1801-1803 states this violates no-actor-mutation-before-confirmation and blocks it only for Galactic Profile sessions. Abandoning chargen leaves the staged credits and any purchases on the actor. Goes through ActorEngine (A-02 satisfied) but not TransactionEngine (A-10) and not through the finalizer (A-15).
findings.intendedOwnership: Starting credits are draft economy state in ProgressionSession; purchases during chargen are a draft cart priced by TransactionEngine and committed atomically with (or immediately after) the finalization plan.
findings.proposedSolution: Owner decision: either (a) chargen store operates on a draft cart in the session and the finalizer emits a TransactionEngine purchase as part of commit, or (b) store opens only after finalization (as Galactic Profile already does). Either way delete _stageStartingCreditsForStore and the duplicated resolveFinalStartingCredits.
findings.alternatives: Keep staging but route through a TransactionEngine "grant starting credits" operation with an abandon-rollback (still mid-wizard mutation).
findings.regressionTests: Test that SummaryStep never calls ActorEngine before finalize; economy builder test for starting credits with and without store purchases.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Chargen: open store, buy, close, change class (budget change), finalize; and abandon after purchase
findings.simplificationBenefit: Removes a parallel credit path and two duplicated reconciliation functions

findings.title: 72 direct actor/owned-item writes across 11 live talent files (all violations)
findings.observed: Per-file classification (all violations of A-02; no exception comment, no world document): sith 25 = 12 own usage/state flags (encounterUses, rapidAlchemy, channelAnger, stolenForm, wildSense), 7 flags on target actors, 6 unsets in lifecycle hooks; consular 12 = 9 own encounter/turn flags + 3 on ally/target actors; force-adept 8 = owned Force power item.update (284), 2 owned weapon flags (511, 529), 1 target flag, 4 own flags; lightsaber 7 = Block/Deflect/Redirect/Riposte own state; sentinel 5 = own state; guardian-spirit 4 = bonus FP pool (91, see F-TAL-007) + 3 usage flags; lightsaber-form-engine 4 = active form/reaction state; jedi-prestige 3 = own flags + prior actor in hook; armor 1 = Shield Expert state; effect wizard 2 = item flags during render (F-TAL-005); approval service 1 = owned talent item.update by GM. Most actions also make a separate ActorEngine call for the cost, so state and cost are two writes.
findings.intendedOwnership: ActorEngine (updateActor with flags paths; updateOwnedItems for owned items), one write per action.
findings.proposedSolution: Introduce a talent-state helper over ActorEngine.updateActor (flags.foundryvtt-swse.talentState.<key>) and migrate file by file starting with sith/consular; fold the paired cost and state into one ActorEngine update; replace power.update/weapon.setFlag/item.update with ActorEngine.updateOwnedItems.
findings.alternatives: ActorEngine.setActorFlag/unsetActorFlag thin wrappers (keeps call shape, still single gate).
dependencies: F-TAL-002 (cross-actor writes need a relay first)
findings.regressionTests: Static guard: no setFlag/unsetFlag/update on actor or owned items in scripts/engine/talent/** except via ActorEngine; extend force-v2-03b-talent-contracts to assert one ActorEngine call per action.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Representative talent from each module used by a player-owned character.
findings.risk: Large surface; flag path changes need a migration or dual-read

findings.title: Effect-wizard _onRender patch writes item flags during render
findings.observed: SWSEItemSheet.prototype._onRender is replaced; the replacement calls maybeAutoOpenCustomTalentWizard, which marks the auto-open consumed with item.unsetFlag/setFlag; a flag write on an owned item triggers another sheet render.
findings.intendedOwnership: UI-only state (wizard presented) in session/client memory, not document flags (OSI performance rule).
findings.proposedSolution: Keep "presented" in a client-side WeakSet/session map; consume the request flag via ActorEngine outside render (on wizard close).
findings.regressionTests: Static guard against document writes inside _onRender/_prepareContext.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Open a workbench-created talent sheet; one render, wizard opens once.

findings.title: Sheet credit edits bypass TransactionEngine
findings.observed: The Add Credits button computes next=max(0,current+amount) and writes system.credits with ActorEngine.updateActor; several templates expose name=system.credits inputs submitted through the sheet form path. TransactionEngine.executeCreditAdjustment exists but is not used. No ledger entry; status feed only.
findings.intendedOwnership: A-10: TransactionEngine is the single credit authority; sheet emits a credit-adjustment intent.
findings.proposedSolution: Route the button and form credit field through TransactionEngine.executeCreditAdjustment (source 'sheet-manual-adjustment'); make the field read-only or intercept it in the form coercion path. Owner decides who may adjust (GM-only vs owner).
findings.alternatives: Keep manual edit as a documented GM-only exception.
findings.regressionTests: Test that sheet adjustments create a TransactionEngine ledger record and that form submit of system.credits is refused or rerouted.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Live V13: player and GM adjust credits from summary/gear tab.

findings.title: Cross-actor flag writes from the acting client without a GM relay
findings.observed: Flags are set on target/ally actors (pendingAfflictions, bondedMount, cripplingStrike, sithCommander.*, Adept Negotiator, pendingMasterAdvisorForcePoint, unsettlingPresence) directly from the client that runs the action. No socket, executeAsGM or GM relay exists in any talent action file. A player normally lacks update permission on enemy actors, so these writes are expected to fail for players; not run in Foundry.
findings.intendedOwnership: ActorEngine with a GM-authoritative relay for documents the user does not own.
findings.proposedSolution: Route cross-actor effects through a GM relay (existing project socket/GM-operation service if present, else a new ActorEngine.requestGmMutation) and store effects as ActiveEffects or target-owned records written by the GM.
findings.alternatives: Store the effect on the source actor and resolve it on the target at read time.
findings.regressionTests: Shim test with a non-owner user asserting the relay is used.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Player uses Affliction / Crippling Strike on a GM-owned NPC.

findings.title: moveEmbeddedDocuments deletes from source before creating on target with no compensation
findings.observed: Source documents are deleted, then target create is attempted; a target failure (permission, validation) loses the item. The only caller, DropService, is orphan-unreferenced (registry), so the path is latent, not live.
findings.intendedOwnership: Cross-actor moves are create-then-delete or transactional (OSI atomicity for transfers).
findings.proposedSolution: Reorder to create on target, verify, then delete on source; or route through applyMutationPlan transactional on both actors. If DropService is confirmed dead, delete it (legacy C) and keep the fixed primitive.
findings.alternatives: Remove moveEmbeddedDocuments until a live caller needs it.
findings.regressionTests: Unit test: target create rejects -> source item still present.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Cross-actor drag between two owned actors with a non-GM user.
findings.simplificationBenefit: Removes a data-loss trap from the gate API.

findings.title: Combat bookkeeping flags written with raw setFlag/unsetFlag, incl. mid-resolution in DamageResolutionEngine
findings.observed: Actor-owned flags (encounter-use counters, stay-up, quick-comeback, threshold-exceeded, emergency patch, action-economy turn state, combat status, pinned actions) are written with actor.setFlag/unsetFlag although ActorEngine.updateActorFlags/unsetActorFlag exist. DamageResolutionEngine.resolveDamage writes them during resolution, before ActorEngine.applyDamage persists HP/CT, so a later failure leaves bookkeeping without damage. Other P-A02 sites in the domain are legitimate: SWSEInitiative Combatant writes (Foundry world docs), poison-engine:126/273 and fire-state-store:292 (world-item fallbacks; fire-state lacks the @mutation-exception comment), attacks.js:1402 (false positive, service call), active-effects-manager.js:61 (token document; legacy token effects array, F-CMB-010 follow-up).
findings.intendedOwnership: ActorEngine (A-02); resolution pure (C-CMB-1).
findings.proposedSolution: Return bookkeeping deltas from resolveDamage and persist them in ActorEngine.applyDamage's single update; route other flag writes through ActorEngine.updateActorFlags. Add @mutation-exception comments on the Combatant and world-item writes.
findings.alternatives: Keep flags but move writes after applyDamage commits.
findings.regressionTests: Failure injection after resolveDamage: no flag changed. Probe P-A02 ratchet for combat.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Stay-up / quick-comeback / threshold-first-exceedance in live combat.
findings.simplificationBenefit: One write per damage event; fewer re-renders.

findings.title: Item sheet writes ActiveEffects and effect-wizard draft flags directly on items
findings.observed: 8 sites write item ActiveEffects / flags with this.item.* regardless of whether the item is embedded in an actor (A-02/A-04); the effect-wizard draft (UI-only state) is persisted on the document. The 7 item.update sites (2456, 2477, 2485, 2510, 2544, 2568, 2809) are world-item fallbacks with @mutation-exception comments (legitimate). Token light updates (2492, 2515, 2582, 2598) are scene-token documents (Foundry-only exception, uncommented).
findings.intendedOwnership: ActorEngine owned-item helpers (A-02); UI-only state in session (OSI).
findings.proposedSolution: Add ActorEngine owned-item ActiveEffect helpers (or route via updateEmbeddedDocuments on the owning actor) and branch like the existing item.update sites; keep wizard drafts in sheet memory/sessionStorage.
findings.alternatives: Treat item-effect edits as documented Foundry-only exception with comments.
findings.regressionTests: Effect create/edit/delete on owned and world items.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Effect wizard on an owned item live.
findings.simplificationBenefit: One mutation path; removes 8 probe hits.

findings.title: Direct actor.setFlag/unsetFlag usage flags in 7 live feat modules
findings.observed: Actor-owned usage/progress flags written directly (violations of A-02; not world docs, no exception comment). combat-feat-damage-rule-resolver uses ActorEngine.updateActor with a setFlag fallback (146). Writes paired with an ActorEngine call (condition-track 309-310, force-point 226-227, meta-resource 1065-1073) are two separate writes, so a failure leaves the state half-applied. Chat-message updates at meta-resource-feat-resolver.js:659,878 are documented supersession writes on ChatMessage documents (legitimate exception, CI-guarded).
findings.intendedOwnership: ActorEngine (single updateActor with flags path, combined with the paired mutation).
findings.proposedSolution: Route EncounterUseTracker through ActorEngine.updateActor({flags.<scope>.<key>}) and fold each paired write into the same ActorEngine update (e.g. gainForcePoints accepting extra flag updates).
findings.alternatives: An ActorEngine.setActorFlag helper with source metadata.
findings.regressionTests: Shim tests asserting a single ActorEngine call per action and no direct setFlag.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Recover action across rounds; Jedi Familiarity once per encounter.
findings.simplificationBenefit: Single mutation path; atomic paired writes

findings.title: force-executor.js: 16 direct flag writes incl. ungated deleteCombat cleanup
findings.observed: Talent-state flags written directly (A-02 violations, no exception comments). shouldSuppressTaintDarkSideIncrease (87) writes inside a predicate. Force Flow grant writes the pool via ActorEngine then a separate setFlag (734): two writes. deleteCombat (1683) runs on every client and issues up to 10 writes per combatant (non-owners fail; one error aborts the loop on that client). Contrast force-power-hooks.js isResponsibleGm.
findings.intendedOwnership: ActorEngine; responsible-GM lifecycle.
findings.proposedSolution: Gate deleteCombat with isResponsibleGm(); batch the cleanup into one ActorEngine.updateActor with -=flag deletions per actor; fold paired writes.
findings.regressionTests: Shim test: two users, one cleanup update per actor.
findings.foundryAcceptance: End combat with GM and player connected.

findings.title: Advisory analytics and Mentor memory written directly to actor flags
findings.observed: Probe reported 24 sites. 8 are false positives (ReasonFactory.create in SuggestionExplainer.js:308/326/334, SuggestionReasonEngine.js:49/257/630, ClassDomainReasonEngine.js:295, attribute-planner.js:158). 16 are real actor setFlag/unsetFlag writes of advisory metadata (no items, system fields or credits). 15 carry '@mutation-exception: metadata'; SuggestionService.js:621 has none (wrapped in ShellMutationGuard instead). ActorEngine.updateActorFlags exists but forces recalcAll, which is a plausible reason for the bypass. Runtime-executed today: SelectionRecorder, SuggestionService._setSuggestionState, mentor-memory. Not executed: SuggestionStateService/AnchorRepository (F-MEN-002), WishlistEngine (only orphan wishlist-ui), mentor-dialogues setters (F-MEN-012).
findings.intendedOwnership: ActorEngine owns actor mutation (A-02/OSI); one suggestion-state service owns advisory flags.
findings.proposedSolution: Owner decides whether advisory metadata flags are a documented A-02 exception class. If yes: record it in A-02 / repo-structure.md and route all MEN flag writes through one SuggestionStateService. If no: add an ActorEngine flag path that skips recalcAll for declared non-derived metadata keys and route through it.
findings.alternatives: Move suggestion analytics off the actor entirely (client-local or user flags) since it is per-player UI history.
findings.regressionTests: Source test: no actor.setFlag/unsetFlag in scripts/engine/suggestion or scripts/engine/mentor outside the chosen service.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Level up and open Mentor chat; verify flags written once and no recalculation storm.
findings.simplificationBenefit: One persistence owner instead of four.

findings.title: SuggestionStateService uses flag scope 'swse' instead of the system id
findings.observed: NS = 'swse' while system.json id is 'foundryvtt-swse'. Foundry validates flag scopes against the system id and active modules, so getFlag/setFlag('swse', ...) is expected to throw (caught and logged in the writers; getState at :155 is not wrapped). Same scope used by unreachable ArchetypeAffinityEngine ('flags.swse.archetypeAffinity'). Currently masked by F-MEN-002.
findings.intendedOwnership: All system flags under 'foundryvtt-swse'.
findings.proposedSolution: Technical defect fix: use the system id constant. Do before enabling F-MEN-002 option (a).
findings.alternatives: Delete the service if F-MEN-002 option (b) is chosen.
findings.regressionTests: Unit test asserting SuggestionStateService scope equals system id.
findings.foundryAcceptance: FOUNDRY_ACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED: confirm the scope error in a live client before/after.

findings.title: Minion modules write owner/minion flags directly from a createItem hook; minion talent flags are write-only uncited rule text
findings.observed: MinionManager.applyTalent/removeTalent/_removeStaleFlags call owner.setFlag / minion.setFlag / unsetFlag directly (8 sites), triggered from the follower createItem/deleteItem hooks. The written flags (minionTacticalAbilities, minionTalentRegistry, minionTalentBenefits) have no reader outside the module. MINION_TALENTS holds hand-written rule paraphrases (e.g. Bodyguard II, Fear Me) without book/page.
findings.intendedOwnership: Minion bookkeeping as a domain service via ActorEngine.updateActorFlags; rule text from talent items/registry, not hard-coded.
findings.proposedSolution: Move MinionManager to scripts/domain/followers/ and route writes through ActorEngine (batched per actor). Owner decides whether the unconsumed flags are needed; if not, delete them (redundant-state). Do not use MINION_TALENTS descriptions mechanically until source-verified.
findings.alternatives: none
findings.regressionTests: Test that adding a minion talent performs one ActorEngine write per actor.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Live V13: Crime Lord minion talents.
findings.simplificationBenefit: 8 direct writes removed; possibly dead state removed.

findings.title: NPC damage hydration mutates owned items from createActor/ready hooks without ActorEngine
findings.observed: On every createActor (GM) and on ready (world scan), item system/flags are rewritten with actor.updateEmbeddedDocuments(render:false). This is migration-like behavior running at every load.
findings.intendedOwnership: ActorEngine owned-item helpers; one-time migration through the migration framework.
findings.proposedSolution: Route through ActorEngine.updateOwnedItems; move the ready scan into a versioned migration (runs once), keep createActor hydration for imports only.
findings.alternatives: none
findings.regressionTests: Test that a second ready does not write.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Live V13: world load time with many NPCs.

findings.title: Draft persistence via raw setFlag in two parallel stores, including UI step position
findings.observed: Chargen persists the draft twice: SessionStorage (flags foundryvtt-swse.progression.<mode>.session, debounced write-behind, semantic dedupe) and ChargenPersistence (flags foundryvtt-swse.chargen.checkpoint on every forward step exit). Both call actor.setFlag/unsetFlag directly. The snapshot includes currentStepId, so navigation alone causes an actor document update (updateActor hooks, sheet re-render). Completion marker also raw setFlag. Draft data in flags is legitimate durability, but bypasses ActorEngine without an exception comment.
findings.intendedOwnership: One draft store behind ActorEngine flag helper (or a documented Foundry-only exception comment), excluding UI-only position from change detection.
findings.proposedSolution: Merge ChargenPersistence into SessionStorage (it already carries recovery data); write through ActorEngine.updateActorFlags with a guardKey or annotate as documented exception; exclude currentStepId/timestamps from the dedupe key so navigation does not write.
findings.alternatives: Persist drafts in a user flag or client storage keyed by actor id (no actor update hooks at all).
findings.regressionTests: tests/progression-session-persistence-writebehind.test.mjs extended: navigation-only change produces no write; resume works from single store.
findings.risk: Low-medium (existing saved checkpoints need a read fallback)

findings.title: Telekinetic Savant/Prodigy text and slot rule hard-coded in a runtime patch, diverging from canonical reference text
findings.observed: The patch replaces picker description/benefit/prerequisite text for two talents with in-code strings and filters the ForcePowerStep Prodigy resolution (suppressProdigyOnlyRetroactiveSlot). The in-code Prodigy text says the extra power must have the [Telekinetic] descriptor and adds a Wisdom-increase clause; the canonical reference (FUCG p.88) says it must be one of the powers affected by Telekinetic Savant. Which text/behavior is authoritative is a rules question; the audit does not decide it.
findings.intendedOwnership: Talent text in talent data (talents domain); Prodigy entitlement in FeatGrantEntitlementResolver / force-suite-resolution.
findings.proposedSolution: Record a register entry (DEFERRED_RULES_REVIEW) with both texts; after a ruling, move text into data and the slot rule into the entitlement resolver; delete the patch.
findings.regressionTests: Force Training with/without Move Object, with Prodigy, at chargen and on later WIS increase.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Force power step with Telekinetic Prodigy

findings.title: Activated species abilities post gameplay chat directly (12 sites)
findings.observed: Every activation result is rendered by ChatMessage.create with inline content instead of the swse-chat service; state writes in the same engine go through ActorEngine.
findings.intendedOwnership: scripts/chat/swse-chat.js

findings.title: 18-file static import cycle between derived calculators, combat-roll-math/combat-stat-rules, ModifierEngine and ActorEngine
findings.observed: Four loops close the SCC: (1) level-split -> utils/hardening (for warnIfMixedTracks) -> ActorEngine -> DerivedCalculator -> level-split; (2) ModifierEngine -> WeaponsEngine -> combat-roll-math -> ModifierEngine; (3) combat-roll-math -> RageEngine -> ActorEngine -> DerivedCalculator -> ModifierEngine -> WeaponsEngine -> combat-roll-math; (4) DerivedCalculator -> ranked-skills-engine -> skill-resolution-layer -> SkillState -> ActorEngine, and ActorEngine <-> missing-prereqs-tracker. The pivots are read-side modules (hardening, RageEngine, SkillState, missing-prereqs-tracker) that also contain write helpers importing ActorEngine statically. Runtime works because all bindings are used at call time, not module evaluation.
findings.intendedOwnership: Prepare-phase calculators depend only downward (infrastructure, data, ModifierEngine); the mutation gate depends on calculators, never the reverse.
findings.proposedSolution: Split read helpers from writers at the four pivots: move warnIfMixedTracks out of utils/hardening.js (or make hardening import ActorEngine lazily only in its restore helper); split RageEngine predicates (read) from rage start/end (write); split SkillState reads from its ActorEngine writes; have missing-prereqs-tracker receive ActorEngine by injection. Separately break ModifierEngine -> WeaponsEngine by having WeaponsEngine register weapon modifiers as a ModifierEngine source (inversion) rather than ModifierEngine importing it (global CR-05).
findings.alternatives: Accept cycles and add a census ratchet (A-P3) so no new edges join the SCC.
findings.regressionTests: Add a census check asserting the derived-calculator subgraph has no path to actor-engine.js; existing derived golden tests must stay green.
findings.simplificationBenefit: Derived calculators become testable without the mutation gate; one SCC shrinks.
findings.risk: Import-order regressions (TDZ) if a split module is evaluated before its dependency; verify with full CI.

findings.title: 6-file chat <-> roll <-> damage-packet cycle through a feat patch module
findings.observed: SWSEChat imports the roll card model, which imports damage-packet-builder (for "offer damage roll"), which imports SkillFeatRuntime from a runtime-patches module, whose resolver posts chat via SWSEChat/RollEngine.
findings.intendedOwnership: Chat is a leaf: renders card models passed to it.
findings.proposedSolution: Have callers build the card model (or pass shouldOfferDamageRoll as data) so swse-chat does not import combat; move SkillFeatRuntime out of the patch module.
findings.regressionTests: Census: no cycle containing swse-chat.js.

findings.title: Composition outside the root and two hook-registration mechanisms
findings.observed: Side-effect imports compose the hotfix layer and progression patches; HooksRegistry (ids, priorities, 35 registrations) coexists with 501 raw Hooks.on/once sites, so hook order and ownership are not inspectable in one place.
findings.intendedOwnership: index.js explicitly calls each installer; one hook-registration API.
findings.proposedSolution: Replace side-effect imports with explicit calls in index.js; adopt HooksRegistry for new hooks and add a census listing of raw Hooks.on sites per domain (no mass rewrite).
findings.regressionTests: Static test: no side-effect-only imports outside index.js.

findings.title: Follower domain authority lives in an app module; engine imports it
findings.observed: FollowerCreator (1,163 SLOC, 16 consumers) owns derivation from owner level and lifecycle; AllyAssignmentService dynamically imports it, noting it cannot be loaded in the Node harness.
findings.intendedOwnership: Follower derivation/lifecycle in scripts/domain/followers/ (pure + ActorEngine); apps keep UI.
findings.proposedSolution: Extract updateFollowerForOwnerLevel and lifecycle methods into a domain service; FollowerCreator becomes the UI over it.
findings.alternatives: none
findings.regressionTests: Node test of the extracted derivation without Foundry UI shims.
findings.simplificationBenefit: Testable follower authority; removes engine->app import.

findings.title: Hotfix layer composed by a hidden side-effect import chain
findings.observed: A module described as "Exposes a macro menu for Squad Actions talent" side-effect imports the whole hotfix layer and two progression-finalizer patches; registration happens at module evaluation (before init) and its order relative to other patches depends on index.js import order.
findings.intendedOwnership: Composition root (index.js) calls explicit registration functions in a documented order.
findings.proposedSolution: Until patches are folded: move the imports into index.js as explicit calls inside init with a comment listing order dependencies; remove side-effect imports from squad-actions-init.js.
findings.regressionTests: Test that squad-actions-init has no side-effect imports.

findings.title: 11-file import cycle progression engine <-> mentor dialogues <-> suggestion is closed by one unused import
findings.observed: mentor-dialogues.js imports ProgressionEngine (unused) -> progression.js -> progression-engine-instance.js -> SuggestionService -> SuggestionEngineCoordinator -> SuggestionEngine -> SuggestionScorer -> mentor-dialogues.js (getMentorForClass). Removing mentor-dialogues.js:1 breaks this SCC; SuggestionService<->Coordinator and SuggestionEngine<->Coordinator mutual imports remain inside mentor-suggestion.
findings.intendedOwnership: Mentor/suggestion are advisory providers below progression orchestration (A-P1).
findings.proposedSolution: Delete the unused import at mentor-dialogues.js:1 (and F-PRG-005).
findings.regressionTests: P-A07-static-cycles probe count drops by one SCC; mentor tests.

findings.title: 11 engine->UI imports in talent action modules
findings.observed: Nine modules import SwseDialogV2 and two import the Force Alchemy workbench app; lightsaber exposes LIGHTSABER_TALENT_IO as a seam already.
findings.intendedOwnership: Engine receives choices through an injected prompt port (as LIGHTSABER_TALENT_IO does).
findings.proposedSolution: Generalize the LIGHTSABER_TALENT_IO pattern into a talent prompt port registered by the UI layer.
findings.regressionTests: Census probe P-A07 count reduction.

findings.title: Engine to UI: crew assignment service opens a dialog; pure modules misplaced under UI directories
findings.observed: VehicleCrewAssignmentService builds HTML and calls SWSEDialogV2.prompt inside the service (real violation). crew-resolver.js, weapon-station-mapping.js and effect-intent-engine.js contain no DOM access; they are domain logic in UI directories (layering-only probe hits).
findings.intendedOwnership: Engine returns candidates; sheet/controller presents the picker and calls assignCrew.
findings.proposedSolution: Move the picker (content + prompt) to scripts/sheets/v2/vehicle-sheet/vehicle-crew-assignment-controls.js; relocate crew-resolver and weapon-station-mapping to scripts/domain/vehicles/, effect-intent-engine to scripts/engine/effects/ (path moves, imports rerouted).
findings.alternatives: Inject a prompt function into the service.
findings.regressionTests: Existing tests/phase6-vehicle-crew-assignment.test.mjs plus a dependency test asserting no scripts/engine/** import of scripts/apps|sheets|dialogs for these files.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Live V13: assign crew via picker.
findings.simplificationBenefit: Removes 4 of 6 vehicle A-07 probe hits.

findings.title: All 31 code-bearing domains form one dependency cycle; no domain can be tested or reasoned about in isolation
findings.observed: Domain-level strongly connected component of size 31 (domainCycles). 9 file-level static cycles (52 files), the largest coupling actor derived calculators with combat math (B-ACT F-ACT-001). Several cycles are closed by unused or re-export imports (B-PRG, B-EQP).
findings.intendedOwnership: ENGINE-ARCHITECTURE §4 dependency direction (APPROVED); A-P1 layering (PROPOSED).
findings.proposedSolution: First remove the cheap cycle-closers identified in domain findings (unused imports, re-exports, dead writers). Then adopt A-P1 layers and track upward edges in dependency-matrix.md as a ratchet. Do not restructure beyond that until waves 2-4 have reduced the graph.
findings.alternatives: Accept the SCC and document allowed peer edges per domain; lower effort, keeps coupling.
findings.regressionTests: Full rolling suite; import-graph diff showing removed edges.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Smoke load of a world (no import errors).
findings.simplificationBenefit: Enables isolated testing and safe deletion; reduces load-order hazards.
findings.risk: Medium; module-evaluation order changes can surface init bugs.

findings.title: Six engine->UI imports in combat engines
findings.observed: 3 static (panel renderer -> sheet adapter, temptation service -> dialog, CombatUIAdapter -> chat bridge), 3 dynamic dialog imports. panel-renderer and ui/CombatUIAdapter are presentation modules located under engine/.
findings.proposedSolution: Move presentation modules out of engine/combat; inject dialog callbacks for the services.
findings.alternatives: Reclassify paths only.
findings.regressionTests: P-A07 ratchet.

findings.title: weapon-runtime 5-file static import cycle via canonicalFeatSlug re-export
findings.observed: ability-selector imports attack-consumer (shapeOfWeapon); attack-consumer imports proficiency-resolver, talent-identity and weapon-runtime-resolver, which import canonicalFeatSlug back from ability-selector (a re-export of scripts/utils/canonical-ability-identity.js).
findings.proposedSolution: Import canonicalFeatSlug from scripts/utils/canonical-ability-identity.js in proficiency-resolver and talent-identity; cycle disappears without moving code.
findings.alternatives: Move shapeOfWeapon to attack-shape.js.
findings.regressionTests: build-census cycle check / existing weapon-runtime tests.

findings.title: Mutual games<->holonet dependency; Holonet is a second session creator
findings.observed: Holonet imports GameSessionStore and GameSessionMaterializer and writes sessions directly. Games import Holonet notification services (8 edges vs 12).
findings.intendedOwnership: Games owns sessions; Holonet owns messaging.
findings.proposedSolution: Expose one games-owned invite API (see F-GAM-001) and have games emit hooks that Holonet listens to instead of importing it.
findings.regressionTests: Census dependency recount.

findings.title: HolonetStorage imports ShellMutationGuard (UI)
findings.observed: Settings writes are wrapped only to silence the shell's dev warning.
findings.proposedSolution: Have the shell guard allow-list storage call stacks, or move the guard primitive to infrastructure.
findings.regressionTests: Census P-A07.

findings.title: Engine-to-UI imports
findings.observed: SuggestionService imports ShellMutationGuard only to wrap its own flag write; BackgroundSuggestionEngine imports a pure helper from an app utils file; aurebesh-translator is a re-export stub (legacy D).

findings.title: Engine-layer progression modules import progression UI (15 edges)
findings.observed: Patch files (F-PRG-001) account for 5 edges; the rest are services importing shell/session or reconciler helpers that live under apps/.

findings.title: Three-file static import cycle in the Shipyard ledger
findings.observed: ledger -> effects (EFFECTS) -> runtime-contract (getVehiclePublishedFieldState) -> ledger (readCertifiedInstallations). getVehiclePublishedFieldState is a pure function with no dependencies.
findings.intendedOwnership: C-VEH-1 acyclic: effects and field-state helpers below ledger, runtime-contract above.
findings.proposedSolution: Move getVehiclePublishedFieldState to a new pure module (e.g. scripts/domain/vehicles/vehicle-published-field-state.js) re-exported from runtime-contract; effects imports it directly.
